name: Beyond Compare
tagline: Desktop diff and merge tool for text files, folders, and a long tail of binary and remote formats.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Sold as a perpetual license rather than a subscription, so monthly price is not meaningful.

verdictSummary: Two-pane text diff is a solved problem: a diff library plus Monaco's diff view gets you 80 percent of the daily use case in an afternoon. Folder comparison with size/timestamp/hash rules is also well within one-shot range, and so is a copy-left/copy-right button. What you will not reproduce in a sitting is the long tail: three-way merge with sane conflict handling, FTP/SFTP/S3/cloud browsing as if it were a local folder, and format-aware comparison of Office docs, PDFs, images, MP3 tags, and hex. There is also the awkward fact that free tools already cover most of this, so the DIY build competes with Meld, WinMerge, delta, and your editor's built-in diff, not just with Beyond Compare. Build it if you want a diff tool shaped exactly like your workflow, not because the license is expensive.
coreLoopDIY: An Electron app that compares two files side by side with syntax-highlighted diffs and two folder trees with same/different/orphan status plus copy and delete actions.
requirements: Node 20+ and a desktop OS you can run Electron on
Comfort shipping an unsigned local app to yourself
Nothing else: no accounts, no cloud
whatYouLose: Three-way merge with an actual conflict resolution UI, which is where most homegrown diff tools quietly give up
Remote filesystems treated as local: FTP, SFTP, S3, WebDAV, cloud drives
Format-aware comparison for Office documents, PDFs, images, hex, MP3 tags, and tabular data with configurable key columns
Twenty-plus years of tuning on huge trees, symlinks, permissions, encodings, and line ending weirdness
Shell integration, git difftool/mergetool wiring, and session management that survives restarts
moatNotes: The moat here is not data or network, it is the thousand edge cases of file comparison that nobody wants to re-discover personally.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because it is a one-time license priced like a nice dinner and it has never surprised anyone. People who compare files for a living want the folder sync to be exactly right, the merge to never silently eat a hunk, and the remote browser to work on a sketchy SFTP server at 2am. That is reliability earned over decades, and the alternative to paying is either a free tool with rougher edges or maintaining your own diff app forever, which is a worse trade than it sounds.
notes: The text diff is a weekend; the hex viewer, the SFTP browser, and the three-way merge are the rest of your year.
prompt:
Build a local desktop diff tool called "Compareish". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Electron with TypeScript, Vite for the renderer, React for UI.
- monaco-editor for the side-by-side text diff view (it has a built-in DiffEditor, use it).
- Node's fs/promises plus node:crypto for folder scanning and hashing.
- No database. Persist settings and recent sessions as JSON in app.getPath('userData').

Features that are IN:
1. File compare: pick two files, show them in a Monaco diff editor with syntax highlighting inferred from extension. Toggles for ignore whitespace, ignore case, and word-level vs line-level diff.
2. Editable right pane with a Save button, plus per-hunk "copy to left" and "copy to right" buttons.
3. Folder compare: pick two directories, walk both recursively in a worker thread, and render a single merged tree. Each row is classified as identical, different, left-only, or right-only.
4. Comparison rules: quick mode uses size plus mtime; thorough mode uses a streaming SHA-256. Make this a visible toggle, and show which mode produced the result.
5. Folder actions on selected rows: copy left-to-right, copy right-to-left, delete. Every destructive action goes through one confirm dialog that lists the exact paths.
6. Filters: glob include/exclude patterns, a "hide identical" switch, and a persisted default exclude list of .git, node_modules, .DS_Store.
7. Double-clicking a "different" folder row opens that pair in the file diff view.
8. Keyboard: next/previous difference, swap panes, refresh scan.

Explicitly OUT of scope, do not attempt:
- Three-way merge, FTP/SFTP/S3/cloud browsing, Office/PDF/image/hex/MP3 comparison, auto-update, code signing.

Quality bar: handle unreadable files and permission errors by marking the row as an error rather than crashing the scan, stream files larger than 50 MB instead of reading them into memory, and show a progress bar with a cancel button during scans. Write a README with run and build commands, and a .env.example only if you actually need a variable.
